pipeline.gate: this contract — semantic checks; grade VALID required

admission_boundary.rule: A VerifiedGraph does not automatically update B. Grade VALID is a necessary but not sufficient condition for topology admission.
admission_boundary.gate: existing CommitAuthority / XulGate commit path in src/kuhul/xul_gate.h
admission_boundary.corollary: Importing a GML file at startup (field_dag.load_gml) populates the in-memory overlay; persisting that to B requires an explicit Xul commit.

V1.name: node_id_required
V1.check: Every node block must contain exactly one 'id' attribute. Zero → MISSING_NODE_ID. Two or more → DUPLICATE_NODE_ID.

V2.name: edge_endpoints_required
V2.check: Every edge block must contain exactly one 'source' and exactly one 'target'. Missing either → MISSING_EDGE_ENDPOINT.

V3.name: edge_endpoints_resolve
V3.check: source(e) and target(e) must be integer IDs that exist in the node table of this graph.

V4.name: overlay_id_unique_within_file
V4.check: Within a single GML file, every node must have a unique integer id. Duplicate integers → OVERLAY_ID_COLLISION_INTRA.
V4.note: Cross-file uniqueness is guaranteed by the file-stem namespace @node:gml:{stem}:{id}. field_dag.cpp:29 enforces this. This check validates the intra-file half.

V5.name: stem_ident_safe
V5.check: The file stem derived from the GML filename (lowercase, non-alnum → '_') must not start with a digit. A filename like '123.gml' produces stem '123', which is not a valid ident. Prepend '_' to produce '_123' to form a valid overlay ID prefix.
V5.note: gml_overlay_id = '@node:gml:' + file_stem + ':' + integer. file_stem is declared as ident in the EBNF. Stems beginning with a digit break the ident production. The validator normalises the stem rather than rejecting the file.

R1.name: verb_wins
R1.formal: verb present ⟹ verb wins; relation attribute ignored
R1.check: When both 'verb' and 'relation' are present on an edge, 'verb' takes precedence. 'relation' is silently dropped. Emit warning BOTH_VERB_AND_RELATION_PRESENT.

R2.name: relation_is_candidate
R2.formal: ¬verb ∧ relation present ⟹ relation becomes RelationCandidate (not VerifiedRelation)
R2.check: When only 'relation' is present, its value feeds infer_relation_from_lexical(). The result is a RelationCandidate, not a VerifiedRelation. Emit RELATION_ALIAS_USED.

R3.name: default_weak_association
R3.check: When neither 'verb' nor 'relation' is present, the edge receives @related_to as weak association default.

R4.name: non_canonical_verb_is_candidate
R4.check: If 'verb' value is not in the canonical set defined in src/micronaut/relation_isa.h, the verb is treated as a string literal passed to infer_relation_from_lexical(). The result is a RelationCandidate, not a VerifiedRelation. Emit INFER_CANDIDATE_USED.

R5.name: near_miss_verb_is_not_canonical
R5.check: A verb that is lexically similar to a canonical verb (e.g. '@relateed_to' ~ '@related_to') is a RelationCandidate with a lower confidence score — it is NOT equivalent to the canonical verb. The validator emits NEAR_MISS_VERB alongside INFER_CANDIDATE_USED. Confidence of the inferred candidate must not be promoted to 1.0.
R5.law: Representation → Relevance → Candidate → Verification, not → Truth

G1.name: coordinates_finite
G1.check: x, y, z must be finite IEEE-754 floats. NaN and Inf are rejected.

G2.name: coordinate_vector_complete
G2.check: If any of x/y/z is present, all three should be present. A partial vector (e.g. only x, y) gets a default of 0.0 for the missing component with a warning.

VerifiedRelation.definition: Canonical verb, exact case-sensitive string match against src/micronaut/relation_isa.h

RelationCandidate.definition: Output of infer_relation_from_lexical() or 'relation' alias. Must pass Ch'en verification before use in B.
RelationCandidate.confidence: < 1.0; assigned by infer_relation_from_lexical() based on lexical similarity
RelationCandidate.path: Candidate → Ch'en → Xul before B update

relation_authority.law: Representation → Relevance → Candidate → Verification — not → Truth
relation_authority.corollary: A near-miss verb is a RelationCandidate with reduced confidence, not a VerifiedRelation with a typo. No silent promotion.

grade.PARSED: Syntactically valid per gml.khanary.ebnf. ParsedGraph produced. No semantic guarantees.
grade.VALID: All FATAL and ERROR checks pass. VerifiedGraph produced. WARNINGs permitted.
grade.ADMITTED: VerifiedGraph accepted into B' via Proposal → Ch'en → XCFE → XulGate. This grade is assigned by the Xul commit path, not by this validator.

id_required_not_in_syntax.observation: node 'id' and edge 'source'/'target' are described as required in comments but not enforced by the EBNF (zero-or-more node_attr).
id_required_not_in_syntax.resolution: Semantic validator checks V1, V2, V3. Grammar remains permissive for ingestion; the validator enforces semantic requirements. No EBNF change needed.

verb_relation_precedence.observation: The 'verb wins over relation' rule is semantic, not in the EBNF.
verb_relation_precedence.resolution: Checks R1, R2 enforce this at the validator layer.

relation_verb_catch_all.observation: relation_verb production includes a string catch-all, so @relateed_to parses cleanly and reaches infer_relation_from_lexical().
relation_verb_catch_all.resolution: Checks R4, R5 classify the result as RelationCandidate with reduced confidence. relation_authority law prevents silent promotion to VerifiedRelation.

file_stem_digit_prefix.observation: file_stem is declared as ident in the EBNF (requires letter or underscore prefix), but the derivation rule allows stems starting with a digit (e.g. filename '123.gml' → stem '123').
file_stem_digit_prefix.resolution: Check V5 normalises the stem by prepending '_' and emits STEM_STARTS_WITH_DIGIT. Overlay IDs remain valid idents after normalisation.

float_1_dot.observation: The float production allows '1.' (digits + dot + zero fractional digits) via zero-or-more { digit }.
float_1_dot.resolution: Accepted as valid. No validator action required. Parser must handle it.

escape_seq_passthrough.observation: Unknown escape sequences (e.g. \q) are passed through literally — the prose is ambiguous about whether the backslash is retained.
escape_seq_passthrough.resolution: Parser-layer concern, not validator-layer. Validator receives parsed string values; the escape handling is completed before validation runs.
